name: building-inspector-actions-visual
description: The building inspector acts in place (#1758). A player selects buildings by clicking them in the scene, never opening the Build panel: researches then upgrades a management office (Research gives way to Upgrade; no Building Destroyer needed: the status follows upgrading, operating at tier 2), moves it with the footprint placement tool armed straight from the inspector, and demolishes a freight warehouse holding hauled ore through the confirm that names the ore lost. The hauling prefix is hauling-gate's own.

steps.description: Staffed opening (#551) with a generous cushion: the hauling prefix below, three placed buildings, a Wrecking Rascal, research and an upgrade all draw on one balance. The prefix up to the tick 60 step is hauling-gate's own, so the freight warehouse (building #1) ends up holding hauled ore before the inspector steps start.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:2 depth:6 start:20,20 diameter:0.089
steps.description: #553: shrunk from the original rows:3 cols:3 (9 holes) to 2x2 (4 holes) and spacing tightened to 2m — this file's whole point is hauling dispatch, not drilling, so the plan only needs to produce enough on-ground fragments to prove auto-haul works, at a workload the staffed roster's driller lands quickly. The click drags the (20,20)-(22,22) rectangle at 2m spacing to compute the declared 2x2. depth corrected from 8 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged. diameter:0.089 added (issue #553 shared-mechanism finding, same root cause as rock-fragmenter-breaking.json/nav-*-visual.json): the real grid-tool confirm always sends the panel's own DEFAULT_DIAMETER_M=0.089 (Drill.ts), while an omitted diameter: on this console command fell back to a different console-only default (0.15, mining.ts) -- computeDrillHoleDurationTicks scales drill duration by diameter, so the omission alone kept the drill_rig busy (and paying fuelCostPerTick) for extra ticks in command mode that the real click's grid never spent, a $54 divergence carried into both downstream cash checkpoints below. Confirmed exact: adding the real default reproduces interaction mode's own $79,268 figure precisely.

#553: drain the ordered plan — the staffed driller/drill_rig lands all 4 holes well inside this pad. Bumped from tick 100 (sandbox-measured landing at tick 88) to tick 130 by #1154's fixer round: the drill_rig now needs vehicle clearance (NAV_CLEARANCE_VEHICLE_CELLS=2) to route to a hole, so it can no longer cut through the 1-cell-wide gap between the freight_warehouse's footprint and the map edge the way a clearance-blind point-agent used to — it correctly detours around the building's east side instead, and that detour route happens to pass near the other freshly-purchased fleet vehicles idling by the depot, costing a few more ticks waiting out real (not phantom) vehicle-occupancy contention before rerouting clear. Sandbox-measured new landing: tick 103 for the 4th hole (H3) — 130 keeps the same proportional margin the original tick-88/tick-100 pair had.
Warehouse #1 lands. Unlike hauling-gate there is no spoil heap here: this file only needs ore in the warehouse.

#1820: select the freight warehouse (#1) before any Research Center or Building Destroyer exists. The inspector shows signed money (Research · $5,000, Move · $7,500, Demolish · $4,000, upkeep $10/h), Research is disabled with the inline reason 'Needs a Research Center', and Demolish stays enabled with the note 'The order will wait: no Building Destroyer in the fleet.'

expect.note: Research blocked: no Research Center yet; Demolish still usable with a wait note.

steps.description: #554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

Rally point (#1772 CI): the Fire step's real click path is DETONATE then Fire anyway (PreflightModal: `blast detonate`, then `blast`), and DETONATE orders the crew out of the danger zone (computeDangerZone, here (5,5)-(37,37)) before the shot. The single bare `blast` this step used to be fired without that evacuation, so command mode and the click took two different trajectories from here on: with the crew now gathered around the rally flag, the click's evacuation walks the free drivers out to the zone edge, and the haulers' first loads become ore instead of the barren rock command mode hauled first. Split into DETONATE and Fire anyway, the shape blast-detonate-fire-anyway.json already uses, so both modes arm, evacuate and fire the same way.
Fire anyway, unevacuated: the shot goes off with the charging crew still at the pattern, as the bare `blast` always did -- the vehicle step below counts the two vehicles it destroys.

#553: staffed:true's fleet (drill_rig, debris_hauler, rock_digger, rock_fragmenter and, since #1648, a charging truck) is 5 vehicles -- and the unevacuated blast above destroyed two of them (the drill_rig and the charging truck, both parked inside their own holes' blast radius, #1649), so vehicleCount goes 5 -> 3 -> 4 with this purchase.
#553: staffed:true's roster (driller/blaster/driver/driver, ids 1-5) means this hire is the roster's 6th employee, not its 1st.

Left unmarked: hiring already grants the Rookie starting qualification (ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION in Employee.ts); this only raises the level for the scenario's needs -- the player-facing path is `employee train`. #553: employee 6, not 1 -- staffed:true's roster occupies ids 1-5.

expect.note: the driver already holds driving.truck at level 1 from ROLE_STARTING_QUALIFICATION -- this call is a same-level no-op

steps.description: #553: vehicle 5 (the debris_hauler just bought) and employee 6 (the driver just hired) -- staffed:true's fleet/roster occupy ids 1-4/1-5. #921: the Fleet panel's Assign/Unassign controls were removed from the DOM entirely; vehicles are now claimed automatically by a qualified employee when a vehicle-gated task needs one. `vehicle driver` survives as a scenario/console-only primitive, so this step now runs as a bootstrap command rather than a UI click.

#552: auto-dispatch spawns the haul_debris PendingAction the moment a fragment lands on_ground with a licensed driver and a free hauler available -- there is no manual click gating it any more, so storedMassKg is no longer pinned to 0 here (the driver may already be under way, or even have delivered, well inside this window). Only cash's upkeep drain is still asserted.

#553: idempotent — a no-op ('No pending event or invalid option.') when nothing is pending, resolves one when a timer fired during the tick 10 block above. A bare `tick` refuses outright while an event is pending, so skipping this defensively stalls the tick 20 step below before the driver ever gets to deliver -- sandbox-measured, an event can fire in this window on seed 42, and events.ts's tick command stops dead the instant one fires mid-block, silently short of the requested count.

#552: automatic dispatch hauls the blast's debris on its own; letting the clock run is the whole action. #1530: ore is delivered to the warehouse (storedMassKg), barren rock to the spoil heap (storedSpoilKg). Rally point (#1772 CI): now that both modes arm and evacuate before the shot (see the `blast detonate` step), the haulers' first loads are ore -- the first warehouse delivery lands inside this block (tick ~230) and the heap receives nothing until the warehouse is full (see the tick 80 block below). This step asserts the first delivery happened, not which kind of rock was nearest.

#554: idempotent (resolveEventIfPending — no-op when nothing is pending). tickCommand itself stops early and auto-pauses the instant any event fires mid-window ("Pending event! Resolve it first"), and the earlier charge-order wait above shifts tickCount enough that a spontaneous event now sometimes lands inside the tick 20 window right above, cutting it short before the hauler's fragment-to-depot round trip has a chance to even start. Clearing it here, before the tick 60 step below actually asserts hauling progress, keeps that assertion honest regardless of exactly when the event happened to fire.

Automatic hauling keeps running; cash's continuing upkeep drain is checkable here, and the haulers keep filling the warehouse (~1.0t to ~13.9t at tick 290 on the aligned trajectory). #1722/#1723: ore and spoil are different orders; which lands first depends on which reachable rock bin the hauler weighs first. Asserting stored ore keeps this step about 'hauling keeps delivering'.
Placed from the Build panel's catalog row for research_center; the Build panel is opened with ensurePanel because earlier steps left a different panel up.

expect.note: Confirming placement only queues a construction site (#556); the next step waits for it to land before its id is referred to.

steps.description: Drive the site to completion. Building ids follow completion order, so each building is awaited before the next is ordered: warehouse #1, research_center #2, management_office #3. Speeds up via the HUD's 8x button first.
Placed from the Build panel's catalog row for management_office; the Build panel is opened with ensurePanel because earlier steps left a different panel up.

expect.note: Confirming placement only queues a construction site (#556); the next step waits for it to land before its id is referred to.

steps.description: Drive the site to completion. Building ids follow completion order, so each building is awaited before the next is ordered: warehouse #1, research_center #2, management_office #3. Speeds up via the HUD's 8x button first.

Select the management office (#3) by clicking it in the scene; no Building Destroyer exists in the fleet, and none is needed for the upgrade below (#1875). Its next tier is locked, so the action strip offers Research, not Upgrade.
Queue the research from the inspector's Research action, which shows its cost and duration; the Build panel stays closed.
Wait on the research queue draining; the inspector follows the progress and then swaps Research for Upgrade.

Research done: Upgrade replaces Research in the strip, with no destroyer wait note (#1875). Clicking it orders in-place construction; the inspector keeps following building #3 and Upgrade, Move and Demolish are all disabled while the upgrade is ordered.
Wait until the same id reaches tier 2: the in-place upgrade finished. The inspector status goes from upgrading to operating.
Move arms the footprint placement tool straight from the inspector: the tile picker appears with the Build panel still closed. Pick the new tile and confirm.

The Wrecking Rascal for the demolition below (#1392). Bought only now: the upgrade earlier needed no Building Destroyer (#1875). The Fleet panel replaces the Build panel and clears the scene selection.
Select the freight warehouse (#1), which holds the hauled ore, by clicking it in the scene.

expect.note: storedMassKg is above zero here: the hauling prefix delivered ore.

steps.description: Demolish from the inspector. The confirm names the cost, that nothing is refunded, and the kg of freight ore that would be lost (checked as text in the unit suite; the screenshot shows it). Confirming orders the demolition.
Wait for the Wrecking Rascal to finish; the ore stored in the warehouse is gone with it.
